tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README for AutoTabML Studio's purpose, quick start, feature set, workflow map, and documentation links. It gives the product context needed to interpret the runtime and ML services that follow.

tour.title: Application Runtime
tour.description: The Streamlit entry point initializes settings, navigation, and page rendering, turning the documented workflows into an interactive application. The project manifest supplies the package, dependency, build, and verification settings that make this runtime reproducible.

tour.title: Shared Configuration
tour.description: Configuration enums and models establish the vocabulary and structured settings shared by application workflows. Their high fan-in makes them the foundation for understanding how UI choices reach the data and modeling services.

tour.title: Dataset Intake
tour.description: Ingestion schemas and types define the structured boundary for bringing datasets into the application. The dataset workspace uses those contracts to load, select, persist, and clear data in the Streamlit session.

tour.title: AutoML Experiments
tour.description: PyCaret schemas describe the typed experiment data used by a core modeling backend, while the FLAML service represents an executable AutoML workflow. Together they show the separation between a user's modeling intent and the engine that carries it out.
tour.languageLesson: Python type schemas make cross-module workflow inputs and results explicit, which helps multiple AutoML backends support the same user journey.

tour.title: Foundation Models Workflow
tour.description: The Foundation Models page introduces a dedicated workflow alongside conventional AutoML, coordinating TabFM tabular evaluation and TimesFM forecasting. TabFM persists reusable context and tracking data, while TimesFM prepares series outputs for forecasting and backtesting, so both paths fit into the wider application lifecycle.
tour.languageLesson: A service-oriented Python workflow can keep model-specific evaluation, forecast generation, and persisted context behind focused modules while the page coordinates the user experience.

tour.title: Prediction Evaluation
tour.description: Prediction schemas define typed inputs, options, and results after a model is trained or selected. The scorer evaluates those predictions, completing the main modeling loop with user-facing evidence of model behavior.

tour.title: Persistence and History
tour.description: The SQLite-backed store initializes local metadata storage and delegates domain operations to repositories. Registry and history services then preserve model metadata and summarize tracked experiments, including results from the workflows already introduced.

tour.title: Security Boundaries
tour.description: Safe HTTP support protects network-facing data acquisition, while trusted-artifact validation limits safe paths and model-loading behavior. These protections apply across ingestion, Foundation Models, and prediction instead of being isolated in a single page.

tour.title: Architecture and Tests
tour.description: The architecture guide connects the module boundaries, data flows, reliability, security, and persistence mechanisms explained in the tour. Foundation-model tests provide focused coverage for the new TabFM and TimesFM paths, while the local smoke test exercises the assembled application.

tour.title: Containerized Deployment
tour.description: The hardened multi-stage Dockerfile packages the locked Python environment and serves the Streamlit UI as a non-root user. Docker Compose adds persistent artifact volumes and an optional MLflow sidecar, exposing the local operational topology.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate dependency installation from the final runtime image, while Compose describes cooperating services, persistent volumes, and local networking.

tour.title: Continuous Integration
tour.description: The GitHub Actions CI workflow automates validation for the code, configuration, and delivery assets described throughout this tour. It closes the onboarding path by showing how the project keeps changes dependable over time.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions organizes automation into triggers, jobs, and ordered steps so validation runs consistently for each proposed change.
